Clinical Notes

PATIENT HISTORY

First-year Physical Therapy student at Benha University (2025-2030), currently training in manual QA and software testing through Egypt's Digital Egypt Pioneers Initiative (DEPI), a national digital-skills program run by the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology.

Comes from a STEM engineering background, with five capstone projects built around real-world failure conditions. Builds and tests software in Java and Flutter, and hardware systems with Arduino from sensor input to user-facing alerts.

Physical Therapy training reinforces the same core skill testing requires: systematic assessment. Observe carefully, isolate the variable, document exactly what's wrong and why, rather than jumping to a fix.

CASE FILE 01

Sign Language Translation Glove

Team project with Hazem Shaker · Competed at the Bibliotheca Alexandrina Science & Engineering Fair, March 2024 (Egypt's regional ISEF qualifier)
Presenting System
A glove-based device meant to translate sign language gestures into readable output, built for a national science fair.
Assessment & Testing
Contributed to building and testing the glove's sensor hardware as part of a two-person team, calibrating sensors against real hand gestures and checking consistency across repeated trials.
Findings
Identified where sensor readings drifted or misfired across different hand sizes and gesture speeds.
Outcome
Glove functioned at the fair; certificate of participation awarded at Egypt's regional ISEF qualifier.
CASE FILE 02

Smart Kitchen Monitoring System

Team project with Hazem Shaker & Ziad Amr · Final STEM capstone, Grade 12, 2024 (Grade: A+)
Presenting System
A kitchen safety unit needing to detect temperature spikes, gas leaks, and smoke in real time, with a live dashboard and a renewable backup power source.
Assessment & Testing
Built and tested an Arduino-based sensor unit (temperature, gas, smoke) against a Python dashboard for live monitoring over Bluetooth; verified sensor-to-dashboard data integrity and solar/battery backup power under sustained load. Led the prototype build with an expanded research and documentation role.
Findings
Solar-charged lithium battery backup held up as a viable renewable power source for continuous monitoring.
Outcome
A fully working prototype: the final capstone project, graded A+.

One of five STEM capstone projects completed during STEM High School, this project focused on real-time sensing, system integration, and reliability under sustained load.

CASE FILE 03

Go Bus Registration — Form Validation Testing

DEPI Software Testing coursework · 2026 (in progress)
Presenting System
A public-facing registration form requiring input validation across Full Name, Phone Number, Password, and related account fields.
QA Approach
Designed test cases using Equivalence Partitioning and Boundary Value Analysis, covering valid, invalid, boundary, whitespace, length, and format-based inputs. Organized the scenarios by field and documented the expected result for each case.
Assessment & Testing
Built reusable test coverage for Full Name, Phone Number, and Password validation, including lower/upper boundaries and representative invalid inputs. The test set is structured for repeatable execution and regression checks.
Findings
Documented the expected validation behavior across boundary and invalid-input scenarios, creating a clear test baseline for execution and future regression testing.
Deliverables
Field-by-field test cases, Equivalence Partitioning scenarios, Boundary Value Analysis cases, steps, test data, and expected results.
View the organized test-case workbook ↗
CASE FILE 04

Children's Ministry Quiz App

Personal project, built to support ongoing volunteer work with a children's ministry · Flutter
Presenting System
An Arabic-language app for running Bible-story quiz competitions with children, needing multi-quiz support and automatic scoring so a class of 12-year-olds can compete without a servant manually grading each answer.
Assessment & Testing
Directed the build and tested the auto-correction and scoring logic (including drag-to-order questions) across multiple quizzes, to confirm answers were graded consistently and correctly regardless of which quiz was loaded.
Findings
An incorrectly ordered sequence is caught and flagged immediately, with the correct step highlighted. Verified scoring stayed accurate and consistent across quiz switches, which is what makes it usable live with a room of kids.
Outcome
Working app, in active use running quiz competitions for his church's children's ministry group.
